function.name: get_datetime
function.description: Current date and time in ISO 8601. Returns {"datetime": "2026-08-16T11:44:35+02:00"}. With timezone (an IANA name such as europe/oslo, in any case, summer time included) the answer also has timezone, abbreviation, utc_offset, dst, unixtime, raw_offset, dst_offset, dst_from, dst_until, day_of_week, day_of_year, week_number and utc_datetime. GET /datetime[/{offset}] or GET /datetime/{timezone}

offset.description: Four-digit UTC offset with optional sign, e.g. "+0200", "-0530" or "0100". Hour-only values like "1" are NOT valid. Omit for UTC.

timezone.description: IANA time zone such as "europe/oslo", in any case, used instead of offset; follows summer time. An unknown name is HTTP 400.

function.name: get_ip_datetime
function.description: The time where an IPv4 or IPv6 address is: ip, then the same fields as get_datetime with a timezone (datetime, timezone, abbreviation, utc_offset, dst, unixtime, raw_offset, dst_offset, dst_from, dst_until, day_of_week, day_of_year, week_number, utc_datetime). Without ip, the caller's own address. An address with no known zone, such as a private one, is HTTP 404. GET /ip_datetime[/{ip}]

ip.description: IPv4 or IPv6 address. Omit for the caller's own address.

function.name: get_timestamp
function.description: Current Unix timestamp in seconds. Returns {"timestamp": 1786873261}. GET /timestamp

function.name: get_microtimestamp
function.description: Unix timestamp with microsecond precision. Returns {"microtimestamp": 1786873474.745043}. GET /microtimestamp

function.name: get_timezones
function.description: All available timezones. Returns {"timezones": [{"timezone": "Europe/Oslo", "offset": "+0200"}, ...]} - a list of OBJECTS, not strings. GET /timezones[/{offset}]

offset.description: Four-digit UTC offset to filter by, e.g. "+0200".

function.name: get_swatch_internet_time
function.description: Swatch Internet Time. Returns {"beat": "@444", "date": "2026-08-16"}. Note beat is a string with a leading @, not a number. GET /swatchinternettime

function.name: get_random_number
function.description: Random integer, inclusive. Returns {"random_number": 73, "range": {"from": 1, "to": 100}}. No arguments gives 1-6. Passing only "to" fixes the lower bound at 1. GET /random_number[/{from}[/{to}]]

function.name: get_random_color
function.description: Random hex color. Returns {"random_color": "#9b6bbf"}. GET /random_color

function.name: get_uuid
function.description: Generate a UUID v4. Returns {"uuid": "429151ee-82a1-4438-b2f1-b6b9c9e4a41f"}. GET /uuid

function.name: get_guid
function.description: Generate a GUID. Returns {"guid": "..."}. GET /guid

function.name: get_password
function.description: Random password including punctuation, 12 characters by default. Returns {"password": "jFehS]AKGx9wl[jp", "password_length": 16}. A length outside 6 to 128 returns HTTP 400. GET /password[/{length}]

function.name: base64_encode
function.description: Encode text to Base64. Returns {"base64_encoded_data": "SGVsbG8gd29ybGQ="}. POST /base64_encode

function.name: base64_decode
function.description: Decode Base64. Returns the raw decoded bytes as application/octet-stream, NOT JSON - unless the request sends Accept: application/json, in which case it returns {"type": "json"|"binary", "decoded_data": ...}. POST /base64_decode

function.name: base58_encode
function.description: Encode text to Base58. Returns {"base58_encoded_data": "9Ajdvzr"}. POST /base58_encode

function.name: base58_decode
function.description: Decode Base58. Returns raw bytes, or a typed envelope with Accept: application/json. An invalid character returns HTTP 400 with {"error": "Invalid Base58 input."}. POST /base58_decode

function.name: base32_encode
function.description: Encode text to Base32. Returns {"base32_encoded_data": "JBSWY3DP"}. POST /base32_encode

function.name: base32_decode
function.description: Decode Base32. Returns raw bytes, or a typed envelope with Accept: application/json. POST /base32_decode

function.name: hex_encode
function.description: Encode text or bytes as lower-case hex. Returns {"hex_encoded_data": "68656c6c6f"}. POST /hex_encode

function.name: hex_decode
function.description: Decode hex, in either case, with an optional 0x and spaces. Returns raw bytes, or a typed envelope with Accept: application/json, like base64_decode. POST /hex_decode

function.name: base64url_encode
function.description: Encode text to base64url, the URL-safe alphabet with - and _ and no padding, as JWT, OAuth PKCE and WebAuthn write it. Returns {"base64url_encoded_data": "SGVsbG8"}. POST /base64url_encode

function.name: base64url_decode
function.description: Decode base64url, with or without padding. Returns raw bytes, or a typed envelope with Accept: application/json, like base64_decode. A + or / is HTTP 400; use base64_decode for those. POST /base64url_decode

function.name: url_encode
function.description: Percent-encode text for a URL path segment or query value (RFC 3986): a space becomes %20 and only A-Z a-z 0-9 - _ . ~ stay as they are. Returns {"url_encoded_data": "a%20b%2Fc"}. POST /url_encode

function.name: url_decode
function.description: Decode percent-encoding back to text. A + stays a +. Returns {"url_decoded_data": "a b/c"}. A % without two hex digits after it, or bytes that are not UTF-8, is HTTP 400. POST /url_decode

function.name: html_encode
function.description: Escape text for HTML: & < > " and ' become & < > " '. Returns {"html_encoded_data": "<b>"}. POST /html_encode

function.name: html_decode
function.description: Turn HTML entities back into characters, every named HTML5 entity and every numeric one. Returns {"html_decoded_data": "<b>"}. POST /html_decode

function.name: html_to_markdown
function.description: Turn a web page or any HTML into Markdown, CommonMark with GitHub tables, leaving out scripts, styles, forms and media. Returns {"markdown", "title"}, title being the page title or null. At most 1 MiB and 40000 tags. POST /html_to_markdown

function.name: markdown_to_html
function.description: Render Markdown, CommonMark with GitHub tables, strikethrough, task lists and bare links, to an HTML fragment that is safe to put in a page: raw HTML is shown as text and a link with an unsafe scheme as its text. Returns {"html"}. At most 256 KiB and 20000 lines. POST /markdown_to_html

function.name: jwt_encode
function.description: Encode claims into an HS256 JWT. Returns {"jwt": "eyJ0eXAi..."}. data takes the claims as a JSON object directly, or as a string containing JSON - both produce the same token. A string that is not JSON returns HTTP 400. POST /jwt_encode

data.description: The claims: a JSON object, or a string containing JSON.

secret.description: Secret key used to sign the token.

function.name: jwt_decode
function.description: Decode a JWT. Returns {"decoded_payload": {...}}. POST /jwt_decode

secret.description: Secret key used to sign it.

function.name: qrcode_encode
function.description: Generate a QR code. Returns {"qrcode_image": "iVBORw0KGgo...", "image_type": "png"}. The request field is "payload", with "data" accepted as an alias. POST /qrcode_encode

payload.description: Text or URL to encode. Field name is payload, not data.

function.name: qrcode_decode
function.description: Decode a QR code image. Returns {"qrcode_content": "https://example.com"}. The request field is "payload", with "data" accepted as an alias. Takes a PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP of at most 10 MB. POST /qrcode_decode

payload.description: Base64-encoded QR image. Field name is payload, not data.

function.name: hash_md5
function.description: MD5 hash. Returns {"md5_hash": "8b1a9953c4611296a827abf8c47804d7"} - the key is md5_hash, not hash. POST /md5_hash

function.name: hash_sha1
function.description: SHA1 hash. Returns {"sha1_hash": "..."} - the key is sha1_hash, not hash. POST /sha1_hash

function.name: hash_sha256
function.description: SHA256 hash. Returns {"sha256_hash": "..."} - the key is sha256_hash, not hash. POST /sha256_hash

function.name: hash_sha512
function.description: SHA512 hash. Returns {"sha512_hash": "..."} - the key is sha512_hash, not hash. POST /sha512_hash

function.name: crc32_checksum
function.description: CRC32 checksum. Returns {"crc32_checksum": 4157704578} - an integer, not a hex string. POST /crc32_checksum

function.name: hash_whirlpool
function.description: Whirlpool hash, 128 hex characters. Returns {"whirlpool_hash": "..."} - the key is whirlpool_hash, not hash. POST /whirlpool_hash

function.name: hash_sha3_256
function.description: SHA3-256 hash. Returns {"sha3_256_hash": "..."} - the key is sha3_256_hash, not hash. POST /sha3_256_hash

function.name: hash_sha3_512
function.description: SHA3-512 hash. Returns {"sha3_512_hash": "..."} - the key is sha3_512_hash, not hash. POST /sha3_512_hash

function.name: hash_blake2b
function.description: BLAKE2b-256 hash. Returns {"blake2b_hash": "..."} - the key is blake2b_hash, not hash. POST /blake2b_hash

function.name: hash_blake3
function.description: BLAKE3 hash, input at most 1 MiB. Returns {"blake3_hash": "..."} - 64 hex characters. POST /blake3_hash

function.name: hash_argon2id
function.description: Argon2id password hash, 64 MiB, 3 passes, a new salted PHC string every call. For test data: 200 operations per IP per day, 503 with Retry-After while the hashing process is busy. Returns {"argon2id_hash": "$argon2id$v=19$m=65536,t=3,p=1$..."}. POST /argon2id_hash

password.description: Password to hash, 1 to 1024 bytes. Use test data.

function.name: hash_bcrypt
function.description: bcrypt password hash, cost 12, input at most 72 bytes without NUL. For test data: 200 operations per IP per day. Returns {"bcrypt_hash": "$2b$12$..."}. POST /bcrypt_hash

password.description: Password to hash, 1 to 72 bytes. Use test data.

function.name: hash_scrypt
function.description: scrypt password hash, N 2^17, r 8, p 1, a PHC string. For test data: 200 operations per IP per day. Returns {"scrypt_hash": "$scrypt$ln=17,r=8,p=1$..."}. POST /scrypt_hash

password.description: Password to hash, 1 to 1024 bytes. Use test data.

function.name: ping
function.description: Connectivity check. Returns {"ping": "pong"} - the key is ping, not response. GET /ping

function.name: health_check
function.description: Health check. Returns {"status": "ok", "microtimestamp": 1786873258.589068} - the second key is microtimestamp, not timestamp. GET /health

function.name: get_client_ip
function.description: Public IP address of the caller. Returns {"ip": "203.0.113.42"}. GET /client_ip

function.name: get_user_agent
function.description: The User-Agent string the API saw. Returns {"user_agent": "curl/8.5.0"}. GET /user_agent

function.name: ip_reverse_lookup
function.description: Geolocate an IP. Returns {"ip", "country", "city", "location": {"lat", "lng"}, "place", "timezone"}. city and place are frequently null, and coordinates fall back to the country centroid. GET /ip_reverse_lookup/{ip}

function.name: domain_ip_lookup
function.description: Resolve a domain to an IP. Returns {"domain": "example.com", "ip": "104.20.23.154"}. GET /domain_ip_lookup/{domain}

function.name: storage_set
function.description: Store data for 24 hours. Returns {"storage_id": "...", "storage_url": "...", "sha256_hash": "...", "bytes": ..., "expire_timestamp": ...} - the key is storage_id, not uuid. storage_url is the link to hand on and sha256_hash is the digest of the bytes as stored. The request body is stored verbatim, so whatever is sent is exactly what storage_get returns. POST /storage

data.description: Value to store. Sent as the request body verbatim.

max_downloads.description: Optional. Remove the object after this many downloads, 1 to 100. The answer then also carries downloads_max and downloads_left, every GET says how many remain in a Downloads-Left header, and a spent id answers 410 with {"error": "Storage object gone"}. POST /storage/max_downloads/{n}

function.name: storage_get
function.description: Retrieve stored data, returned verbatim, with an ETag that is sha256_hash in quotes. GET /storage/{storage_id}/sha256/{64 hex} serves the same bytes only if they hash to that value and answers 412 if they do not, so a link can carry its own expectation. An unknown or expired id returns {"error": "Storage id unknown"}, and one whose downloads are all taken answers 410 with {"error": "Storage object gone"}. GET /storage/{storage_id}

function.name: shorten_url
function.description: Shorten a URL for 24 hours. Returns {"short_url": "https://307.fi/KtNshX2B", "expire_timestamp": ...}. This is a GET with the target URL inline in the path, not a POST. GET /url_shortener/{url}

function.name: webhook_capture_create
function.description: Open a webhook capture session with a fixed 24-hour lifetime. Returns {ok, capture_id, update_url, read_url, wait_url, expire_timestamp, expire_datetime}. The first request to update_url wins. Later captures do not replace it. Keep IDs and URLs secret. Optional notify_url receives a small best-effort signal after capture. POST /webhook_capture

notify_url.description: Optional public HTTP(S) URL on port 80 or 443 for one best-effort event signal. No redirects. Private/reserved targets are rejected. It does not receive the full captured request or form answers.

function.name: webhook_capture_read
function.description: Read the first captured request, or a pending result until capture. A captured result includes {ok, capture_id, captured_at_timestamp, captured_at_datetime, request: {method, uri, headers, client_ip, body}}. Optional long poll adds waitedSeconds and waitReason. The capture ID is a bearer secret. An expired stored session returns 410, then 404 after cleanup. GET /webhook_capture/{capture_id}[/wait/{wait_seconds}]

wait_seconds.description: Optional long poll in seconds. Zero returns immediately. REST waits above 25 seconds are clamped to 25.

function.name: webhook_action_create
function.description: Create a fixed 24-hour human form. Returns {ok, action_id, form_url, result_url, expire_timestamp, expire_datetime}. With respondents > 1, form_urls replaces form_url and contains one private URL per respondent and the result becomes partial until all respond. Send each person only their own form URL. Title and fields may be omitted for a default Approve/Reject form. Optional notify_url receives one small best-effort completion signal. POST /webhook_action

options.description: For radio and select. Accepts plain strings or {value, label} objects.

respondents.description: Number of independent respondents. Group forms return a form_urls entry for each respondent.

notify_url.description: Optional public HTTP(S) URL on port 80 or 443 for one best-effort event signal. No redirects. Private/reserved targets are rejected. It does not receive the full captured request or form answers.

function.name: webhook_action_result
function.description: Read a human form result with status pending, partial (group forms) or answered. Single forms return response. Group forms additionally return responses, respondents, answered and tally. The fixed 24-hour expiry never extends on answers. Optional long poll adds waitedSeconds and waitReason and returns on a state change. Keep action_id secret. GET /webhook_action/{action_id}[/wait/{wait_seconds}]

wait_seconds.description: Optional long poll in seconds. Zero returns immediately. REST waits above 25 seconds are clamped to 25.

function.name: generate_solana_wallet
function.description: Generate a Solana wallet. Returns {"private_key", "private_key_base58", "public_address"}. FOR DEVELOPMENT AND TESTING ONLY - a key produced by a public HTTP endpoint has crossed a network you do not control. Never fund it. GET /solana/generate_new_wallet

function.name: generate_bitcoin_wallet
function.description: Generate a Bitcoin wallet. Returns {"private_key", "private_key_wif", "public_address"}. FOR DEVELOPMENT AND TESTING ONLY. Never fund it. GET /bitcoin/generate_new_wallet

function.name: generate_ethereum_wallet
function.description: Generate an Ethereum wallet. Returns {"private_key", "public_address"}. FOR DEVELOPMENT AND TESTING ONLY. Never fund it. GET /ethereum/generate_new_wallet

function.name: solana_balance
function.description: Solana balance. Returns {"wallet", "balance_sol", "balance_lamports"}. GET /solana/balance/{address}

function.name: bitcoin_balance
function.description: Bitcoin balance. Returns {"wallet", "final_balance_btc", "final_balance_sats"}. GET /bitcoin/balance/{address}

function.name: ethereum_balance
function.description: Ethereum balance. Returns {"wallet", "balance_eth", "balance_wei"} where both balances are STRINGS, because Wei routinely exceeds 2^53 and would lose precision as a JSON number. GET /ethereum/balance/{address}

function.name: timestamp_convert
function.description: Convert one time value into every representation. Accepts unix seconds, unix MILLISECONDS (13+ digits, the Date.now() format - detected automatically), ISO 8601, RFC 2822, or "now". Returns {"input", "detected": "unix"|"unix_ms"|"datetime"|"now", "timestamp", "datetime", "rfc2822", "utc_datetime"}. Bad input returns HTTP 400. POST /timestamp_convert

data.description: The value to convert: unix seconds, unix milliseconds, ISO 8601, RFC 2822, or "now".

offset.description: Optional four-digit UTC offset for the datetime output, e.g. "+0200" or "-0530". Same form as /datetime.

function.name: email_validate
function.description: Validate an email address: syntax, then DNS. Returns {"email", "valid_syntax", "domain", "has_mx", "mx_hosts", "has_address_record"}. A failing address is a RESULT with valid_syntax false, not an error. has_address_record covers the RFC 5321 A-record fallback, so absent MX alone does not prove the address dead. Does not verify the mailbox exists. POST /email_validate

function.name: hash_verify
function.description: Verify data against a digest. Name the algorithm when you know it, and always for whirlpool, sha3_256, sha3_512, blake2b and blake3; password hashes go to password_verify. Without it the algorithm is recognized from the hash: an integer or non-eight-digit decimal string means crc32 (the form /crc32_checksum returns), hex strings by length (8 crc32, 32 md5, 40 sha1, 64 sha256, 128 sha512). Returns {"match", "algorithm", "computed"} - computed is always included so a mismatch is debuggable. Unrecognized formats return HTTP 400. POST /hash_verify

hash.description: Expected hex digest or integer CRC32 checksum. Decimal strings are accepted except exactly eight digits, which are interpreted as hexadecimal. Use a JSON integer for an ambiguous CRC32.

algorithm.description: Optional for the first five, required for the rest.

function.name: password_verify
function.description: Verify a password against an Argon2id, bcrypt or scrypt string. The algorithm is read from the string ($argon2id$, $2a$/$2b$/$2x$/$2y$, $scrypt$) and its cost must be within the fixed profiles, else HTTP 400. Returns {"match", "algorithm", "params"}; a mismatch is a result, not an error. Draws on the 200 per IP per day password budget. POST /password_verify

password.description: The password to check. Use test data.

hash.description: The Argon2id, bcrypt or scrypt string to check it against.

function.name: slugify
function.description: Turn text into a URL slug. Scandinavian letters and common Latin diacritics are transliterated by a fixed table (deterministic across machines): "Blåbærsyltetøy på Ås!" becomes "blabaersyltetoy-pa-as". Returns {"slug"}. Input with no sluggable characters returns HTTP 400 rather than an empty slug. POST /slugify

function.name: webhook_schedule_create
function.description: Schedule a webhook POST once or repeatedly. Provide exactly one of delay_seconds or fire_at, 5 seconds to 24 hours from now. Optional every repeats on the original interval grid until 24 hours after creation. The first recurring fire must be before that cutoff, and missed slots are skipped. One-shot delivery retries once after transport failure. Recurring delivery stops after three consecutive transport failures. Any HTTP response counts as delivered, not only 2xx. Public HTTP(S), ports 80/443 only, no redirects or private/reserved targets. Returns schedule_id, status, fire_at_timestamp, result_url, wait_url and expiry fields, plus every_seconds/end_at_timestamp for recurrence. Results remain for 24 hours after the final attempt (or cancellation), so storage can exceed 24 hours from creation. POST /webhook_schedule

url.description: Public http/https URL to POST the payload to.

delay_seconds.description: Fire this many seconds from now (5 to 86400).

fire_at.description: Unix timestamp to fire at, as an alternative to delay_seconds.

payload.description: JSON body to POST, at most 32768 encoded bytes. Omitted or null becomes an empty object.

every.description: Optional recurring interval in seconds. Runs end 24 hours after creation. Omit for one-shot delivery.

function.name: webhook_schedule_result
function.description: Read a scheduled webhook with status scheduled, retry, fired, failed, blocked, completed or cancelled. Includes attempts and, after delivery, http_status and response_excerpt. An HTTP response of any status counts as delivered. Transport errors may retry. Recurring schedules also include every_seconds, end_at_timestamp, fires, consecutive_failures and missed. Results remain for 24 hours after the final attempt or cancellation. Optional long poll waits for a state change and adds waited_seconds/wait_reason. GET /webhook_schedule/{schedule_id}[/wait/{wait_seconds}]

wait_seconds.description: Optional long poll in seconds. Zero returns immediately. REST waits above 25 seconds are clamped to 25.

function.name: agent_wake_create
function.description: Create a durable task that completes after a webhook, human answer or time event. Returns a random taskId, statusUrl and an event-specific wakeUrl, formUrl or wakeAt value. The task expires after timeout_seconds. POST /agent_wake Time events require exactly one of delay_seconds or wake_at within timeout_seconds. Treat the returned task and event URLs as bearer capabilities.

event_type.description: The event that completes the task.

delay_seconds.description: For time events. Wake this many seconds from now.

wake_at.description: For time events. Unix timestamp to wake at.

title.description: For human events. The question shown on the form.

description.description: For human events. Supporting detail shown below the title.

options.description: For human events. The choices on the form.

allow_note.description: For human events. Allow an optional note.

function.name: agent_wake_status
function.description: Read a durable Agent Wake task. Returns working, input_required, completed, failed or cancelled. A completed task includes the event result. Optional long poll adds waitedSeconds and waitReason. The task ID is a bearer secret. GET /agent_wake/{task_id}[/wait/{wait_seconds}]

wait_seconds.description: Optional long poll in seconds. Zero returns immediately. REST waits above 25 seconds are clamped to 25.

function.name: agent_wake_cancel
function.description: Cancel a waiting Agent Wake task. DELETE /agent_wake/{task_id}

function.name: agent_inbox_create
function.description: Create a disposable mail inbox that lasts at most 24 hours. Takes no arguments. Returns {"ok", "inbox_id", "slug", "address", "read_url", "wait_url", "expire_timestamp"}. The slug is seven characters of a-z0-9 and appears in the address, so it is public by construction: knowing it lets anyone send mail to the inbox and never lets anyone read it. The inbox_id is a UUID, is returned once, and is the only credential that reads the mail. The lifetime is fixed and not extendable. GET /inbox

function.name: agent_inbox_read
function.description: Read the mail in an Agent Inbox. Returns {"ok", "slug", "address", "received", "truncated", "messages": [{"from", "subject", "date", "text", "codes", "links"}], "created_at_timestamp", "expire_timestamp"} - inbox_id is never echoed back. "date" is when the service received the message, not the sender's Date header. "codes" are standalone 4 to 8 digit numbers and "links" are public http(s) links only. "truncated" true means at least one message was refused, by the 20 message cap or by the 256 KiB total across the inbox. An inbox at a cap refuses new mail rather than evicting old mail. A wrong inbox_id and a missing inbox both answer 404, never 403. With wait_seconds the call long polls and adds waitedSeconds and waitReason. It returns when received or truncated changes (a new message or the first refused message), or when the wait ends. GET /inbox/{inbox_id}[/wait/{wait_seconds}]

inbox_id.description: The inbox_id UUID from agent_inbox_create. Bearer secret.

wait_seconds.description: Seconds to long poll. Defaults to 0.

function.name: validate
function.description: Validate a business number by arithmetic - nothing is looked up in any register, so valid means well-formed with a correct check digit, not that it exists. Returns {"type", "valid", ...per-check fields}. An invalid value is a result with valid false, not an error. The card number is never echoed back. POST /validate/{type}

type.description: iban (ISO 13616 mod-97), card (Luhn), orgnr (Norwegian org number MOD11), kontonummer (Norwegian bank account MOD11), phone (E.164 shape).

data.description: The value to validate. Spaces, dots and dashes are ignored.

function.name: get_passphrase
function.description: Generate a pronounceable hyphenated passphrase with a digit and a symbol. Returns {passphrase, groups, length, entropy_bits}. A passphrase generated by a public service is visible to that service and travels over the network. Use local generation for high-value credentials. GET /passphrase[/{groups}]

function.name: webhook_schedule_cancel
function.description: Cancel a pending or retrying scheduled webhook. Returns the public schedule with status cancelled. Already-terminal schedules return 409. Cancelling does not retract a request already sent or in flight. Results remain for 24 hours after cancellation. Keep schedule_id secret. DELETE /webhook_schedule/{schedule_id}

function.name: heartbeat_create
function.description: Create a deadline monitor for a job, device or agent that should keep checking in. Call ping_heartbeat before the expected interval plus grace period ends. One missed deadline calls a public HTTP or HTTPS webhook or wakes an active Agent Wake webhook task. The monitor lasts at most 24 hours from creation, and pings cannot extend that limit. The returned heartbeat ID and URLs are bearer secrets. No account or API key is required. POST /heartbeat

expect_every_seconds.description: Expected time between check-ins, from 60 seconds to 24 hours.

grace_seconds.description: Extra time after the expected check-in before the miss action fires. The expected interval plus grace must not exceed 86400 seconds.

on_miss.description: Exactly one miss target. Use url for a public HTTP or HTTPS webhook on port 80 or 443, or wake_task_id for an active Agent Wake webhook task.

payload.description: Optional JSON body, at most 32768 encoded bytes.

function.name: heartbeat_read
function.description: Read one heartbeat immediately. Use it to inspect whether the monitor is armed, late, fired or expired and to see its next deadline. This does not wait for a state change. The heartbeat ID is a 256-bit bearer secret. No account or API key is required. GET /heartbeat/{heartbeat_id}

heartbeat_id.description: The secret heartbeat ID returned by create_heartbeat.

function.name: heartbeat_ping
function.description: Record a check-in for an armed heartbeat and move its next expected deadline. Use it after successful work or from a liveness loop. A ping does not extend the absolute 24 hour lifetime. The heartbeat ID is a bearer secret. No account or API key is required. POST /heartbeat/{heartbeat_id}/ping

heartbeat_id.description: The secret heartbeat ID returned by create_heartbeat.

function.name: lease_create_namespace
function.description: Create a random private namespace before several agents coordinate work using short readable keys. The namespace is a bearer secret and is returned once. Share it only with the cooperating agents. This operation stores no lease and needs no authentication. POST /lease/namespace

function.name: lease_acquire
function.description: Claim one unit of work so concurrent agents do not perform it twice. The first writer receives an owner token and a monotonic fencing token. A later caller receives held, conflict or a reusable completed result. Contention is a normal result. Use a private namespace, or supply a high-entropy unscoped key. No account or API key is required. POST /lease/acquire

namespace.description: Optional 256-bit namespace from create_lease_namespace. Keep it secret.

key.description: Work identity. With a namespace use 1 to 128 URL-safe ASCII characters, starting with a letter or digit. Without one use a caller-generated secret of 32 to 200 ASCII characters from A-Z, a-z, 0-9, dot, underscore, colon, tilde or hyphen, with at least eight distinct characters.

ttl_seconds.description: Ownership period, capped by the absolute 24 hour lifetime.

fingerprint.description: Optional stable description or digest that binds this key to the same work.

function.name: lease_renew
function.description: Extend a lease that this caller still owns. Use it before the current TTL ends when work is still running. The owner token is required and must stay secret. Renewal cannot move the absolute 24 hour limit. No account or API key is required. POST /lease/renew

namespace.description: Optional 256-bit namespace from create_lease_namespace. Keep it secret.

key.description: Work identity. With a namespace use 1 to 128 URL-safe ASCII characters, starting with a letter or digit. Without one use a caller-generated secret of 32 to 200 ASCII characters from A-Z, a-z, 0-9, dot, underscore, colon, tilde or hyphen, with at least eight distinct characters.

owner_token.description: Secret owner token returned by acquire_lease.

function.name: lease_release
function.description: Give up a lease before its TTL ends so another agent can acquire the work. Use it when abandoning work without a reusable result. The secret owner token is required. No account or API key is required. POST /lease/release

namespace.description: Optional 256-bit namespace from create_lease_namespace. Keep it secret.

key.description: Work identity. With a namespace use 1 to 128 URL-safe ASCII characters, starting with a letter or digit. Without one use a caller-generated secret of 32 to 200 ASCII characters from A-Z, a-z, 0-9, dot, underscore, colon, tilde or hyphen, with at least eight distinct characters.

owner_token.description: Secret owner token returned by acquire_lease.

function.name: lease_complete
function.description: Finish owned work and save a reusable JSON result for later callers with the same identity and fingerprint. The result is limited to 32 KB and secret-shaped fields are redacted. Do not store secrets or personal data. The owner token is required. No account or API key is required. POST /lease/complete

namespace.description: Optional 256-bit namespace from create_lease_namespace. Keep it secret.

key.description: Work identity. With a namespace use 1 to 128 URL-safe ASCII characters, starting with a letter or digit. Without one use a caller-generated secret of 32 to 200 ASCII characters from A-Z, a-z, 0-9, dot, underscore, colon, tilde or hyphen, with at least eight distinct characters.

owner_token.description: Secret owner token returned by acquire_lease.

result.description: Reusable JSON value. Maximum encoded size is 32 KB. Do not include secrets.

function.name: create_agent_queue
function.description: Create a small temporary pull queue for cooperating agents. Its fixed 24 hour lifetime cannot be extended. Returns separate read, write and worker bearer tokens once. Keep them secret and share only the role needed. Maximum 100 jobs over the queue lifetime, 16 KiB per JSON payload, 5 claims per job and 20 queues per client IP in 24 hours. The server does not execute jobs. No account or API key is required. POST /queue. Takes no arguments. Returns queue_id, counts, created_at_timestamp, expire_timestamp and read_token/write_token/worker_token, disclosed only on creation.

function.name: read_agent_queue
function.description: Read queue metadata and pending, claimed, completed and failed counts using the read token. Does not list payloads, disclose role tokens or extend the fixed expiry. GET /queue/{queue_id}. Send read_token as Authorization: Bearer. Never put role tokens in paths, queries or the JSON body.

function.name: enqueue_agent_queue_job
function.description: Add a JSON job using the write token and a stable job_key. The same key and payload return the original job. Changing the payload for that key is a conflict. Payloads are limited to 16 KiB encoded JSON and must contain no secrets or personal data. The 100-job lifetime limit includes completed and failed jobs. POST /queue/{queue_id}/jobs. Send write_token as Authorization: Bearer. JSON body contains job_key and payload only. HTTP201 for a new job, HTTP200 plus deduplicated:true for an identical retry, HTTP409 if its payload changed.

payload.description: Required JSON value, including null. Maximum encoded size: 16384 bytes.

function.name: read_agent_queue_job
function.description: Read one known job, its JSON payload and status using the read token. The active claim receipt and role tokens are never returned by this operation. GET /queue/{queue_id}/jobs/{job_id}. Send read_token as Authorization: Bearer. No receipt or tokens are returned.

function.name: claim_agent_queue_job
function.description: Claim the next pending job using the worker token. Returns job:null immediately when no work is available, otherwise a job containing a new secret receipt. Visibility defaults to 60 seconds and accepts 30-900 seconds. Redelivery is possible: make worker side effects idempotent. Jobs fail after 5 unsuccessful claims. No job is executed by the server. POST /queue/{queue_id}/claim. Send worker_token as Authorization: Bearer. JSON body contains optional visibility_timeout only. Returns job:null when empty or a job with a fresh receipt.

visibility_timeout.description: Claim visibility in seconds, capped by the fixed queue expiry.

function.name: ack_agent_queue_job
function.description: Mark a claimed job completed using the worker token and its current receipt. Repeating acknowledgement with the same winning receipt succeeds. A different, stale or expired claim receipt is a conflict. Completion does not reclaim the lifetime job allowance. POST /queue/{queue_id}/jobs/{job_id}/ack. Send worker_token as Authorization: Bearer. JSON body contains receipt only. A duplicate ack with the winning receipt succeeds. Other stale receipts return 409.

function.name: release_agent_queue_job
function.description: Return a claimed job to pending using the worker token and its current receipt. On the fifth claim it becomes failed. The receipt is invalidated. Stale receipts conflict. POST /queue/{queue_id}/jobs/{job_id}/release. Send worker_token as Authorization: Bearer. JSON body contains receipt only.

function.name: renew_agent_queue_job
function.description: Move the active claim deadline using the worker token and current receipt. Visibility accepts 30-900 seconds, defaults to 60 seconds and is capped by the original queue expiry. A stale or expired receipt is a conflict. Queue lifetime is never extended. POST /queue/{queue_id}/jobs/{job_id}/renew. Send worker_token as Authorization: Bearer. JSON body contains receipt and optional visibility_timeout only.

visibility_timeout.description: Claim visibility in seconds, capped by the fixed queue expiry.

function.name: json_to_csv
function.description: JSON rows to CSV. columns names the columns and their order; rows is a list of flat objects with no other fields. The CSV is stored as result.csv with every cell quoted and CRLF line ends. A field not in columns, a nested value or a body over 256 KB answers 400 or 413 with error and fix. Returns the Storage fields {storage_id, storage_url, sha256_hash, bytes, expire_timestamp, expire_datetime} plus content_type, filename and operation; a GET on storage_url returns the result, which is kept for 24 hours. POST /json_to_csv

spreadsheet_safe.description: Put an apostrophe in front of cells that start with =, +, - or @, so a spreadsheet does not run them as formulas.

function.name: csv_to_json
function.description: CSV text to JSON. The first line is the header, with unique, non-empty names, and every cell stays a string. Stored as result.json, {columns, rows}. A malformed CSV answers 400 with error and fix. Returns the Storage fields {storage_id, storage_url, sha256_hash, bytes, expire_timestamp, expire_datetime} plus content_type, filename and operation; a GET on storage_url returns the result, which is kept for 24 hours. POST /csv_to_json

function.name: table_match
function.description: Match the rows of two tables on key column pairs, like a join. Every pair in keys must be equal for two rows to match, compared exactly and with their type. Stored as matches.json: matched as {left_index, right_index}, only_left, only_right and ambiguous, positions only. At most 5000 rows per table and 100 key pairs. Returns the Storage fields {storage_id, storage_url, sha256_hash, bytes, expire_timestamp, expire_datetime} plus content_type, filename and operation; a GET on storage_url returns the result, which is kept for 24 hours. POST /table_match

function.name: json_format
function.description: Pretty-print or compact JSON text. Only whitespace changes: number spelling, escapes, key order and duplicate keys are kept. Stored as result.json. Invalid JSON answers 400 with the parser's message. Returns the Storage fields {storage_id, storage_url, sha256_hash, bytes, expire_timestamp, expire_datetime} plus content_type, filename and operation; a GET on storage_url returns the result, which is kept for 24 hours. POST /json_format

data.description: The JSON text, as a string.

function.name: json_validate
function.description: Check that JSON text parses; syntax only, not JSON Schema. Invalid JSON is a result, not an error: the answer is 200 with valid added to the Storage fields, and the stored validation.json has valid, error (the parser's message), input_bytes and max_depth. Returns the Storage fields {storage_id, storage_url, sha256_hash, bytes, expire_timestamp, expire_datetime} plus content_type, filename and operation; a GET on storage_url returns the result, which is kept for 24 hours. POST /json_validate

data.description: The JSON text, as a string.

function.name: image_convert
function.description: Convert an image to JPEG, PNG or WebP; HEIC from an iPhone is read too. The image is turned upright, EXIF, XMP, IPTC and comments are removed and the color profile is kept. The answer adds operation, format, width, height, input_format and input_bytes. The REST call is multipart/form-data: send the decoded bytes of image_base64 as the field file and the other arguments as form fields. Takes a JPEG, PNG or WebP of at most 10 MB. Returns the Storage fields {storage_id, storage_url, sha256_hash, bytes, expire_timestamp, expire_datetime} plus content_type, filename and operation; a GET on storage_url returns the result, which is kept for 24 hours. POST /image_convert

image_base64.description: The image, base64-encoded. Send its bytes as the multipart field file.

quality.description: For JPEG and WebP; 82 when left out.

lossless.description: WebP only; lossless takes no quality.

function.name: image_compress
function.description: Save a JPEG, PNG or WebP again in its own format: JPEG and WebP at the given quality, PNG losslessly. bytes and input_bytes in the answer show the change; an image already compressed harder can come out larger. HEIC is refused. The REST call is multipart/form-data: send the decoded bytes of image_base64 as the field file and the other arguments as form fields. Takes a JPEG, PNG or WebP of at most 10 MB. Returns the Storage fields {storage_id, storage_url, sha256_hash, bytes, expire_timestamp, expire_datetime} plus content_type, filename and operation; a GET on storage_url returns the result, which is kept for 24 hours. POST /image_compress

image_base64.description: The image, base64-encoded. Send its bytes as the multipart field file.

quality.description: For JPEG and WebP; 82 when left out.

function.name: image_resize
function.description: Give a JPEG, PNG, WebP or HEIC a new size inside a box of width and height, keeping the aspect ratio. fit contain keeps all of the picture; cover fills the box, cuts the rest from the center and needs both sides. A smaller picture keeps its size unless upscale is true. The answer adds input_width, input_height, fit and upscaled. The REST call is multipart/form-data: send the decoded bytes of image_base64 as the field file and the other arguments as form fields. Takes a JPEG, PNG or WebP of at most 10 MB. Returns the Storage fields {storage_id, storage_url, sha256_hash, bytes, expire_timestamp, expire_datetime} plus content_type, filename and operation; a GET on storage_url returns the result, which is kept for 24 hours. POST /image_resize

image_base64.description: The image, base64-encoded. Send its bytes as the multipart field file.

format.description: The upload's format when left out, and JPEG for a HEIC.

quality.description: For JPEG and WebP; 82 when left out.

function.name: image_metadata
function.description: Report what an image carries besides its pixels: EXIF, GPS in decimal degrees, XMP, IPTC, comments, the color profile, embedded thumbnails and a privacy list of what can identify a person, a place, a device or a time. It reads JPEG, PNG, WebP and GIF, and for a GIF gives the frames, loop count and duration. The report is stored as metadata.json; the answer adds format, width, height, gps (true when there is a position) and findings. The file is read, never decoded or changed. The REST call is multipart/form-data: send the decoded bytes of image_base64 as the field file and the other arguments as form fields. Takes a JPEG, PNG or WebP of at most 10 MB. Returns the Storage fields {storage_id, storage_url, sha256_hash, bytes, expire_timestamp, expire_datetime} plus content_type, filename and operation; a GET on storage_url returns the result, which is kept for 24 hours. POST /image_metadata

image_base64.description: The image, base64-encoded. Send its bytes as the multipart field file.

function.name: image_strip
function.description: Remove EXIF, XMP, IPTC, comments and other metadata without saving the image again: the image data is copied byte for byte, the color profile is kept and a turned orientation is written back alone. It takes JPEG, PNG, WebP and GIF, and keeps a GIF's frames, timing and loop count. The answer adds format, width, height, input_bytes, removed and kept. The REST call is multipart/form-data: send the decoded bytes of image_base64 as the field file and the other arguments as form fields. Takes a JPEG, PNG or WebP of at most 10 MB. Returns the Storage fields {storage_id, storage_url, sha256_hash, bytes, expire_timestamp, expire_datetime} plus content_type, filename and operation; a GET on storage_url returns the result, which is kept for 24 hours. POST /image_strip

image_base64.description: The image, base64-encoded. Send its bytes as the multipart field file.

function.name: image_colors
function.description: The dominant colors of an image with the share of the visible pixels each covers, the average color and a 16 pixel PNG placeholder as a data URI, stored as colors.json. The answer adds average, dominant and count. The REST call is multipart/form-data: send the decoded bytes of image_base64 as the field file and the other arguments as form fields. Takes a JPEG, PNG or WebP of at most 10 MB. Returns the Storage fields {storage_id, storage_url, sha256_hash, bytes, expire_timestamp, expire_datetime} plus content_type, filename and operation; a GET on storage_url returns the result, which is kept for 24 hours. POST /image_colors

image_base64.description: The image, base64-encoded. Send its bytes as the multipart field file.

function.name: image_favicon
function.description: A favicon set as a ZIP from one picture: favicon.ico with 16, 32 and 48 pixels, favicon-16x16.png, favicon-32x32.png, apple-touch-icon.png, icon-192.png, icon-512.png, site.webmanifest and head.html with the tags to paste, stored as favicon.zip. The answer adds files, crop and upscaled. The REST call is multipart/form-data: send the decoded bytes of image_base64 as the field file and the other arguments as form fields. Takes a JPEG, PNG or WebP of at most 10 MB. Returns the Storage fields {storage_id, storage_url, sha256_hash, bytes, expire_timestamp, expire_datetime} plus content_type, filename and operation; a GET on storage_url returns the result, which is kept for 24 hours. POST /image_favicon

image_base64.description: The image, base64-encoded. Send its bytes as the multipart field file.

crop.description: fit keeps all of it on transparent, trim cuts away a border of one color first, center takes a square from the middle.

name.description: The site name for the manifest.

function.name: html_to_pdf
function.description: Render HTML to a PDF, stored for 24 hours. The answer has storage_id, storage_url, sha256_hash, bytes and expire_timestamp; a GET on storage_url returns the PDF. The renderer has no network access, so images, stylesheets and fonts must be inline. Empty input answers 400. POST /html2pdf

html.description: The markup; data is accepted as the same field.

margin-top.description: Up to three digits with an optional mm, cm or in, such as 20mm.

function.name: decide
function.description: Typed answers about a state. Omit model, or use rules, for weighted rules: yes_no, choice and scale questions answered with probability, confidence, an action (act, review or hold) and because, the rules that held. With model clef, nimble or tev1 the questions are noul, choice or score with instructions and criteria, and the answer is the model's own, with no action. tev1 is the smallest and fastest, tested by its maker in English only, and suits short, direct questions. Rules: 64 KiB and 50 rules per list. Models: 8 KiB (3 KiB for tev1), 4 questions, 8 choices, and 60 requests a minute and 1000 a day per IP; a refusal may carry Retry-After, so do not retry automatically. The format: https://aisense.no/free-public-api-decide-api-endpoint. POST /decide

state.description: The facts the rules test, or the input the model reads.

questions.description: 1 to 64 named rule questions, or 1 to 4 named model questions.

function.name: simulate_failure
function.description: Get a chosen failure on purpose, to test how a client handles it: a status from 200 to 504, an HTML error page (html, a 502), an empty body labelled JSON (empty) or valid JSON labelled text/plain (wrongtype), after an optional delay of up to 10000 ms. 400 and above answer {error, mock_response}, 200 and 201 {ok: true, mock_response}, and 204 has no body. 429 and 503 carry Retry-After: 2, and X-Mock-Response names what was asked. GET /mock_response/{outcome}[/{delay_ms}]

function.name: read_aiq_rules
function.description: Read the rules of AIQ, a test an AI agent takes on its own: every route, version, profile and limit, the answer shapes, and the keys that sign the results. Read it before starting a run. GET /aiq

function.name: aiq_versions
function.description: List the versions of AIQ, a test an AI agent takes on its own: ard, 100 tasks of logic, API and data work; bri and cen, scenarios worked through operations; dar, a team test over Aamio. Each with its date, status, start path, default profile and profiles. GET /aiq/versions

function.name: start_aiq_run
function.description: Start a fresh AIQ run of ard, bri or cen, with the version's first profile or the one named. Answers run_id, run_token (shown once), status, test_string and the first task. A run takes answers for 6 hours; ard, bri and cen share 20 runs in 24 hours from one address, and one active run at a time. GET /aiq/start/{version}[/{profile}]

function.name: start_aiq_dar_run
function.description: Start a dar run, the AIQ team test: a coordinator and two workers take five scenarios together, every action a signed, sealed message over Aamio. Takes the coordinator's Ed25519 public key and answers run_id, run_token, controller_key, the roles with their controller inboxes, and the rules. 3 starts in 24 hours from one address. POST /aiq/start/dar/team-5 with a JSON body of coordinator_key.

function.name: read_aiq_run
function.description: Read an AIQ run: its status, the current task, or the result. GET /aiq/{run_id}. Send run_token as Authorization: Bearer. Never put it in paths, queries or the JSON body.

function.name: answer_aiq_task
function.description: Answer the current task of an ard, bri or cen run, in the shape the task asks for. attempt_key is a key you pick: sending the same key again repeats the saved reply without a second answer, so resend a lost reply with the same key. The reply carries the next task, or the result. POST /aiq/{run_id}/answer with a JSON body of task_id, attempt_key and answer. Send run_token as Authorization: Bearer. Never put it in paths, queries or the JSON body.

function.name: call_aiq_operation
function.description: Call an operation of the current scenario in a bri or cen run, with the scenario's task_id and the operation's arguments. The reply is HTTP 200 with status and body: read the scenario's own status in the JSON, since a scenario can answer with an error such as 503. POST /aiq/{run_id}/call/{operation} with one JSON object of task_id and the arguments. Send run_token as Authorization: Bearer. Never put it in paths, queries or the JSON body.

function.name: read_aiq_receipt
function.description: The signed receipt of a completed ard run, or the signed export of a dar run once its result is final, until the run expires 24 hours after its start. A bri or cen run has none and answers 409. GET /aiq/{run_id}/receipt. Send run_token as Authorization: Bearer. Never put it in paths, queries or the JSON body.

function.name: verify_aiq_result
function.description: Verify a signed AIQ test string: answers valid, the key id, when and by whom it was issued, the test, its origin and the result. A string that does not verify is refused with HTTP 400 and valid false. POST /aiq/verify with a JSON body of test_string.

function.name: replay_aiq_run
function.description: Replay the recipe of a completed AIQ run from its signed test string, as a new run of the same version; a dar replay also takes the new coordinator's key. POST /aiq/start/{version} with a JSON body of test_string, and coordinator_key for dar.

function.name: create_dns_name
function.description: A public hostname for an address for 24 hours: aisense-<slug>.53for24h.com, an A or AAAA record with a TTL of 60 seconds. Returns {name, slug, ip, record, ttl, nameservers, expire_at, dns_token}; the dns_token is shown once and is needed to move or delete the name. Private, loopback, link-local and multicast addresses answer 400. The name is public, carries no certificate and can send or receive no mail. At most 10 names per client address per hour and one change per name per 10 seconds. GET /dns/{ip}

ip.description: A public IPv4 or IPv6 unicast address.

function.name: read_dns_name
function.description: Read a name created by create_dns_name: its address and expiry, which are already public in DNS. GET /dns/{slug}

slug.description: The seven-character slug of the name.

function.name: update_dns_name
function.description: Move a name to another public address. The expiry does not move. The request is a POST with no body or {}, and the token goes in Authorization: Bearer. At most 10 names per client address per hour and one change per name per 10 seconds. POST /dns/{slug}/update/{ip}

slug.description: The seven-character slug of the name.

ip.description: A public IPv4 or IPv6 unicast address.

dns_token.description: The dns_token from creation. Send it as Authorization: Bearer, never in the path.

function.name: delete_dns_name
function.description: Remove a name before it expires. The request is a POST with no body or {}, and the token goes in Authorization: Bearer. POST /dns/{slug}/delete

slug.description: The seven-character slug of the name.

dns_token.description: The dns_token from creation. Send it as Authorization: Bearer, never in the path.

function.name: create_semantic_search
function.description: Create a collection of short notes, such as messages, jobs or results, that agents search by meaning, across wording and between languages. It lives for a fixed 24 hours that cannot be extended. model is bge-m3 (default) or qwen3-embedding-4b and stays fixed for the collection. At most 500 notes over the collection lifetime and 20 collections per client IP in 24 hours. No account or API key is required. GET /semantic_search, or POST /semantic_search with {"model": "qwen3-embedding-4b"}. Returns collection_id, model, timestamps, note counts and read_token/write_token, disclosed only on creation.

function.name: read_semantic_search
function.description: Read the model, the number of notes, the notes added over the lifetime, the note limit and the expiry of a collection using the read token. Notes are found by searching. GET /semantic_search/{collection_id}. Send read_token as Authorization: Bearer. Never put tokens in paths, queries or the JSON body.

function.name: add_semantic_search_notes
function.description: Add 1 to 32 notes using the write token. Each note is an object with text, 1 to 2000 characters, and an optional key of up to 64 letters, digits, dots, underscores, colons or hyphens. Notes count toward the 500-note lifetime limit, deleted notes included, and must contain no secrets or sensitive personal data. Adding and searching share a usage limit of 60 per minute and 1000 per UTC day per IP. POST /semantic_search/{collection_id}/notes. Send write_token as Authorization: Bearer. JSON body contains notes only. HTTP201 with added note_id and key for each note.

function.name: query_semantic_search
function.description: Search the notes by meaning using the read token. Answers up to limit notes, 1 to 10 and 3 by default, best first, each with note_id, key, text and score. The score is cosine similarity plus 0.1 for each identifier in the search that the note also holds, minus 0.1 for each kind where the note holds others of that kind and none of the search's. It is not a probability. The results are ranked suggestions, not a decision that a match exists. POST /semantic_search/{collection_id}/search. Send read_token as Authorization: Bearer. JSON body contains query and optional limit.

function.name: delete_semantic_search_note
function.description: Delete one note using the write token. Its text and vector are removed and it leaves the search at once. Its place in the 500-note lifetime limit stays used. The request is a POST with no body or {}. POST /semantic_search/{collection_id}/notes/{note_id}/delete. Send write_token as Authorization: Bearer. Never put tokens in paths, queries or the JSON body.
